name: Blueberry
lede: Blueberry is the color of the fruit, a deep violet-[[blue|blue]]; as a color word it is recent.

sections.title: A fruit and its color
sections.body:
Pastoureau notes a plant model behind the medieval link between green and youth: fruit is green before it becomes red (cherries, strawberries, raspberries), then blue or black, blueberries among them [1]. The idea of freshness was central to the medieval sensibility, and it helped tie green to youth [1].

The books say almost nothing else about the color itself. The pigment literature mentions blueberry only in a reference on its anthocyanins, plant pigments [2]. As a color name, blueberry is modern: in Google Books the adjective peaks in the 2010s [3]. That makes it a young word for an old fruit, with no dye or pigment history we can source [2][3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The color is rare in paint. It appears in 0.01% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive (3 paintings, as photographed) [4]. It is rarer than 79% of the named colors we track [4].
